page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-96 is a compute-focused instance configuration featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz, backed by 54 MB of L3 cache and support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators such as AES and SHA-NI. The instance is paired with 96.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per virtual core. It does not include integrated local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel throughput across multi-threaded computational workloads. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress testing, Clang software compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving throughput reaching 60.55 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth uncached exceeds 318 GB/sec, supporting high throughput in data-intensive integer and cryptographic routines. In contrast, single-threaded metrics, including single-core stress tests and Geekbench scores, fall within average tiers, reflecting standard per-core execution speeds rather than ultra-high individual clock frequencies.

The 1.0 GB per vCPU memory provisioning represents an architectural tradeoff, prioritizing raw CPU thread density over per-core memory capacity. As local storage is absent, all operational persistence relies on external cloud block storage. This resource distribution yields favorable cost efficiency for compute-bound applications that fully utilize 96 concurrent threads without requiring expansive in-memory buffers.

The n2-highcpu-96 instance is well suited for highly parallelized workloads such as continuous integration build pipelines, code compilation, video encoding, ray tracing, and high-throughput static web serving fleets.
